body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Friday, August 14, 2026, and we’re starting the day with a look at the night that was — from a high-speed DUI south of the Grapevine to a welfare check for a woman seen crying for help in a red pickup. Today’s high will reach 95°, with an overnight low around 67°, and air quality is moderate at AQI 59. Let’s get you caught up.

## The Kern Overnight

The night opened quietly enough, with a traffic unit requested around 9:10 p.m. for the 600 block of 33rd Street. But by 9:23 p.m., dispatchers were sending city units to White Lane for a road-rage disturbance involving a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both repeatedly stopping and blocking the eastbound roadway. The incident drew no further update on the air. Around 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street; officers took the report, and no arrests were announced. The night’s most serious call came around 11:34 p.m., when Bakersfield police broadcast an attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller described an older-model red truck at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace — a male hanging out the driver’s window, a female crying and saying she needed help. The truck was last seen traveling southbound, and the broadcast went out citywide. Fire crews were comparatively quiet, handling a residential alarm on Greenview Lane around 11 p.m. that amounted to nothing and a vehicle accident that drew an engine, battalion, and rescue unit before the air went quiet. Just after midnight, a theft from a space at a mobile home park on Barlow Road was reported, with a loss estimated near $3,900 and a suspect named. And shortly before 3 a.m., a traffic collision in the Flying J truck stop parking lot at Frazier Park saw a burgundy Freightliner hit by a red Peterbilt, with the other party denying involvement. CHP was investigating the hit-and-run claim as the feed moved on.

## Today's weather

Today’s high will reach 95° under sunny skies, with a low tonight around 67°. It’s currently 77° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and no active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at AQI 59.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** Bakersfield Christian High School’s football team is looking to right the wrongs of last year’s state title loss as they gear up for the new season. The Eagles are working to build on their experience and come back stronger, with a focus on teamwork and determination.

**23ABC tells us that** Bakersfield’s police and fire chiefs presented their Fourth of July reports during a Friday meeting, revealing both progress and ongoing concerns about fireworks-related incidents in the city. Kevin Albertson, Chief of the Bakersfield Fire Department, said the holiday brought serious consequences for people across the state. A total of 106 citations were issued by the Bakersfield Police and Fire departments combined in relation to the holiday. Compared to 2025, fire-related responses to both departments dropped 6% in 2026. Despite the decrease, residents and officials say more work remains. Bakersfield City Councilman Eric Arias said stronger policies are in the works.

**23ABC also shares** that Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, traveled to San Diego on August 12 to celebrate the public release of a federal best practices toolkit aimed at addressing addiction treatment within the homeless community — a project he helped build from the ground up. Baldovinos was among roughly 22 professionals from across the country who gathered in Washington, D.C., in the spring to work with the Trump administration, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the Department of Health and Human Services, and the nation’s drug czar to develop the toolkit. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics including program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development.

**KGET 17 reports that** Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that would place Kern and dozens of other counties in a new state, separate from coastal California. Kern County District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores said the effort is about making sure the region’s industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. An analysis presented to the board found the proposed inland state would account for only about 15 percent of California’s current real GDP. CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart said that number tells a stark story about what separation would actually mean for the region.

## Something good

Bakersfield and Tehachapi airports will receive a portion of the $109 million federal aviation funding. This funding will support improvements and upgrades to local airport infrastructure.

## Coming up this week

This afternoon, the Special Safe and Healthy Neighborhoods Committee meets at 1 p.m., followed by the Keep Bakersfield Beautiful Committee at noon and the Special Laws and Legislation Committee at noon. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation And Traffic Safety Committee meets at noon, the Historic Preservation Commission convenes at 4 p.m., and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission meets at 2 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board meets at 10 a.m. On Thursday, August 20, the Planning Commission meets at 5:30 p.m. And this weekend, the Fox Theater will host PEPPER With CYDEWAYS on August 14, Los Yonic’s Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio on August 22, Rodney Carrington on August 27, CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on August 28, Willie Barcena on August 29, and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix on August 29.
